nodes.name: Payload Valid?

nodes.name: Wait Before Step 2
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 days — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

# Remind upcoming appointments: Google Sheets & Slack

**Pattern:** Reminders & Follow-ups · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers follow-ups work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack and Telegram.

It moves through 21 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Stamp & Shape Contact
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Segment Audience
6. Step 1 — Welcome (Telegram)
7. Tag for Slow Nurture
8. Wait Before Step 2
9. Converted Already?
10. Step 2 — Value Nudge (Telegram)
11. Mark Converted — Stop Drip
12. Update Drip Status
13. Stamp Completion Time
14. Persist Run Metadata
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Load Previous Snapshot
18. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
19. Summarize Run Stats
20. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
21. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing follow-ups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Stamp & Shape Contact → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Segment Audience → Step 1 — Welcome (Telegram) → Tag for Slow Nurture → Wait Before Step 2 → Converted Already? → Step 2 — Value Nudge (Telegram) → Mark Converted — Stop Drip → Update Drip Status → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for follow-ups
- Follow-ups sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Google Sheets
- Follow-ups work where "Stamp & Shape Contact" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Follow-ups work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for follow-ups, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 24 nodes of this follow-ups build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 24 nodes in this follow-ups build
- The pause before Google Sheets is durable — a follow-ups run survives a restart
- Every follow-ups run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every step checks 'Converted Already?' before sending — a drip campaign that keeps emailing someone who already bought is the fastest way to burn trust. The Wait node's durable resume state (via `webhookId`) is what lets a multi-day wait survive an n8n restart instead of being held only in memory.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a 4th drip step with its own wait/exit-check pair.
2. Manually flip a test record's status to 'converted' mid-drip and confirm the ladder stops sending.
3. Shorten the wait durations so the full ladder runs in minutes instead of days, for testing.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your follow-ups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

**Do not log**
follow-ups payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
